lesson.title: Draw it: charts
lesson.subtitle: Pictograms, bar charts, and charts that are fair

video.title: Draw it: charts
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Salma — the maths teacher (main character)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: My chart; Mangoes win!; Not from zero. Ms Salma beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: I asked my class which fruit they like most, and drew a chart. Mangoes won by a mile! Then Musa said: Miss, your bars don't start at zero.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: draw charts from your data, and check that they're fair.

scenes.visual: One big value: 2 pupils, for each picture.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A pictogram uses little pictures. Each picture stands for some votes: one picture, two pupils. Always write what one picture means.

scenes.visual: A bar chart that draws itself: 12, 7, 9 (Votes for each fruit).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A bar chart: taller means more
scenes.narration: A bar chart uses bars. The taller the bar, the more votes. Every bar has the same width, a label underneath, and starts at zero.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Tallest: oranges, 12; Shortest: bananas, 7; Oranges: 5 more.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: To read a bar chart, find the tallest bar and the shortest. Then compare: oranges got five more votes than bananas.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! In a pictogram, one orange picture means two pupils. There are four pictures. How many pupils is that?

scenes.visual: One big value: 8, Four pictures, two pupils each.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Eight. Four pictures, two pupils each: two, four, six, eight.

scenes.visual: Two columns: “Unfair” (Starts at 5; A bar left out) and “Fair” (Starts at 0; Every answer shown).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Charts must be fair. Bars start at zero, or a small difference looks huge. And every answer gets its bar, even the small ones.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Look for odd values; A jump to zero and back; A chart shows it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Look for odd values too. If a soil reading jumps to zero and straight back, something went wrong. On a chart, it jumps out.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Soil readings; Find the red dots; Leave them out.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, a week of soil readings from the school garden. Find the red dots: the readings that can't be right. Tap “Leave them out”, and see the lowest reading change.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Which of these charts is fair?

scenes.visual: Summary card: Say what one picture means; Tallest bar: the most; Bars start at zero. Takeaway bar: A fair chart shows every answer, from zero.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The one with bars from zero, and every answer shown. Remember: a pictogram says what one picture means. The tallest bar has the most. And a fair chart starts at zero.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Your tally from lesson 1; A title and labels; Bars from zero. Ms Salma beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: turn your tally from the first lesson into a bar chart. Give it a title and labels. And start the bars at zero!

checkpoints.prompt: One orange picture means two pupils. There are four pictures. How many pupils?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — four pictures, two pupils each: eight.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — each picture means two pupils, so count in twos: two, four, six, eight.

checkpoints.prompt: Which of these charts is fair?

options.text: Bars that start at zero, with every answer shown

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — bars from zero show the real differences, and every answer gets its bar.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — bars that don't start at zero make small differences look huge, and hiding answers hides the truth.
